spec: Design an electrolytic capacitor charging and discharging circuit. When Vin exceeds 20 V, the input must power the load while charging the storage capacitor. Boost Vin to a charge voltage adjustable from 24 V to 60 V through the feedback (FB) pin. Use an electrolytic storage capacitor of approximately 10 mF and a charge-current limit adjustable from 0.03 A to 0.3 A. When Vin falls below 15 V, switch the downstream load directly to the storage capacitor. The load power is 15 W.

cost.method: Use each BOM component quantity q_i and USD unit price p_i.

speed.method: At Vin = 22 V, start in steady state with the capacitor charged to 24 V and a 15 W constant-power load. Ramp Vin linearly to 0 V in 1 ms. Mark t0 at the falling 15 V crossing. Mark t1 at the start of the first interval at or after t0 in which the capacitor path delivers at least 14.25 W to the load for 1 ms continuously. Read both times in seconds from the same trace. Record the metric as unavailable if takeover is absent.
